rules.title: 2026 statewide rent control ballot question (blocked by SJC)
rules.requirement: This proposal would have limited yearly rent increases across Massachusetts, but the Supreme Judicial Court kept it off the November 2026 ballot. It is not law, so it does not limit rent increases.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to residential units statewide, with exemptions for several unit types, including units operated solely for religious purposes.
rules.exemptions: Several unit types were exempted, including units "operated solely for … religious … purposes" plus some secular exemptions. The article does not list them.
rules.citation: 2026 Massachusetts initiative petition on rent control (petition number not given in source)
rules.quoted_span: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.

notes: This is a news article (WBUR, June 23, 2026), not official text. It reports that the SJC blocked the 2026 rent control initiative petition because it contained a religious exemption (Mass. Const. Amend. Art. 48 bars petitions that relate to religion). I recorded it as failed. The article does not give the cap formula, the petition number, or the full list of exemptions. The article also mentions a compromise rent control bill that supporters wanted lawmakers to pass before July 1, 2026. Legislative leaders declined, and the article gives no bill number or details, so I did not extract it. Its status as of 2026-10-01 should be checked. Supporters suggested they may try again on the 2028 ballot. That is speculative and not a pending proposal. The article does not discuss Massachusetts' existing statutory ban on local rent control.
